# Absolute value, minimum and maximum

The magnitude of a floating-point value and the smaller or larger of two.

<h2 id="abs"><code>Abs</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Abs(x: float64) -> float64
pub func Abs(x: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the absolute value of `x` at `float32` precision.
Widening a finite `float32` to `float64` and narrowing its magnitude back is exact. As with the wide overload,
either signed zero becomes `+0.0`, either infinity becomes positive infinity, and a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                              | Summary                                                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Abs(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the absolute value of `x`.                        |
| `pub func Abs(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the absolute value of `x` at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Abs.rux#L13)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description                       |
| ---- | --------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | value whose magnitude is returned |

**Returns**: `x` without its sign

<h2 id="max"><code>Max</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Max(a: float64, b: float64) -> float64
pub func Max(a: float32, b: float32) -> float32
```

Selects the larger of `a` and `b`.
A NaN loses to a number, so one NaN returns the other argument and two NaNs return a NaN. When both arguments are
zeros, a positive zero wins.

| Overload                                          | Summary                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Max(a: float64, b: float64) -> float64` | Selects the larger of `a` and `b`.                        |
| `pub func Max(a: float32, b: float32) -> float32` | Selects the larger of `a` and `b` at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Max.rux#L13)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description             |
| ---- | --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `a`  | `float64` / `float32` | first value to compare  |
| `b`  | `float64` / `float32` | second value to compare |

**Returns**: the larger non-NaN value, or a NaN when both arguments are NaNs

<h2 id="min"><code>Min</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Min(a: float64, b: float64) -> float64
pub func Min(a: float32, b: float32) -> float32
```

Selects the smaller of `a` and `b`.
A NaN loses to a number, so one NaN returns the other argument and two NaNs return a NaN. When both arguments are
zeros, a negative zero wins.

| Overload                                          | Summary                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Min(a: float64, b: float64) -> float64` | Selects the smaller of `a` and `b`.                        |
| `pub func Min(a: float32, b: float32) -> float32` | Selects the smaller of `a` and `b` at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Min.rux#L13)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description             |
| ---- | --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `a`  | `float64` / `float32` | first value to compare  |
| `b`  | `float64` / `float32` | second value to compare |

**Returns**: the smaller non-NaN value, or a NaN when both arguments are NaNs
